Decoding the hex in the EXECVE argument a2 of the first bash process: "63617420207C2078617267732062617368202D6320" translates to "cat  | xargs bash -c " — a pipeline piping content into xargs that executes bash -c, and the PROCTITLE confirms "bash -c cat | xargs bash -c". This is a command-execution pattern where piped input is fed to a shell, commonly used to run dynamically constructed or obfuscated commands. The processes run as root with auid unset (no login session attribution), which is consistent with a remote or scripted execution path rather than an interactive user.
